summaries.summary: The customer walk-in return submission slice is substantially correct. I diffed ReturnConfirmation.tsx vs ReturnConfirmationDesktop.tsx: the entire handleSubmit logic (eligibility math, totalRemainingQty full/partial detection including rentPrice=0 items via type-based counting, WIN- deterministic id, legacy-ticket cleanup excluding walkinId per the race fix, pickup-vs-walkin routing with partial+pickup forced into the walk-in queue, double-submit ref guard) is character-identical in both files; ReturnItems/ReturnItemsDesktop also match (deny-by-default ownership, -1 sentinel sanitization, per-item max clamp). Server side, store.php correctly scopes walkinReturns GET/POST/DELETE to the customer's own orders, rejects cross-owner ticket overwrite, fires FCM only when the FOR UPDATE-read row is new/tombstoned (stage-recheck patches do not re-notify), and OrderBus push intentionally sends no X-Base-Rev while patch is OCC-guarded with 409 rebase (verified against backendSync ConflictError and the retry loop). Photos are externalized to /api/uploads or R2 URLs before upsert. Remaining defects found: customer photos are silently dropped from the permanent returnInspections record because StaffDashboard filters to data:-URLs only (post-externalization regression), the flow is not gated by isReturnEligible so undelivered orders can be "returned" from the OrderDetail button, cross-method re-submission leaves the other pipeline's state behind, and three lower-severity issues (desktop 修正する divergence, WIN- id squatting authz asymmetry, success alert without flush()).

The two-stage core is correct: reception patch records receptionReturnDate/fieldInspector and hands counted→expected off to the recheck ticket (counted reset to 0 for independent re-count); the recheck queue displays reception counts via expected; finalize restores only good units (counted minus non-shortage defects) capped by stockDeductedQty budget with correct draw-down/backstop propagation; missing/broken flow into computeCompensationCharge (clamped, idempotent extraCost injection on -R blocks); over-count is clamped by computeReturnSplit; the finalizingRef guard holds; and OCC does not block the flow (updateOrder patches are local-synchronous, 409s rebase in background — the whole-items-field overlay on rebase is the known C29 field-level LWW class, not a new failure). However I found two real corruption bugs: the new multi-device restock guard (liveAlreadyRestored) resolves the WRONG order via an undefined===undefined firestoreId match — it reads whatever order is newest, so restock is silently skipped right after any partial-return finalize (whose -R order carries stockRestored:true) while the order is still stamped stockRestored, permanently losing stock; and the 再検品 (reinspect) button re-runs the full finalize pipeline on already-finalized cycles, double-restocking and closing continuing partial-return orders or wiping items on closed orders when re-counted short.

The core money math of partial/walk-in returns is correct: I traced computeReturnSplit → finalizePartialReturn → getOrGenerateInvoiceBlocks → invoice rendering with worked examples and confirmed -R bills per-unit from rentalStartDate to the reception date × returned qty, the continuing order bills remaining qty to the original end, guarantee fee is billed exactly once (zeroed on -R), compensation/fuel land only on the finalized -R (C15), C7 proration is numerically exact (round(newNatural × override/oldNatural), tier-B crossing included), C9 block ids are unique, C6 preservation runs in both updateOrder paths, 2-3 sequential cycles produce gap-free non-overlapping cumulative billing, and tax uses consistent per-block trunc with order totals equal to block sums. Three real defects remain: (HIGH) -R orders' blocks are born and persisted with status "paid" (billing.ts:606 × status "返却済" set before block generation), so returned-portion rent + 弁償費 never appear as 未入金/延滞 in AdminInvoices; (MED) the min-chargeable-days basis flips between 3 and 10 days when a split separates vehicle from non-vehicle items, over-charging the persisted blocks and making the monthly PDF's line items disagree with its own totals; (LOW) an early full-return close silently drops manual extraCosts/paid marks on trailing months eliminated from the new span.

This slice is correct for the audited invariants. A concrete 3-cycle simulation (qty 10 → return 4 w/1 broken → return 3 w/1 missing → return rest) yields total restock 8 = physically-returned good units, with the stockDeductedQty budget drawing down 10→7→5 correctly because the continuing order is the same record patched in place (the -R split is the new, inert record); over-count is clamped by the budget so Σrestored ≤ Σdeducted always holds. OCC 409-rebase is strictly no-worse than pre-OCC: a stale admin drawer save reverts items (incl. draw-down) and status because handleSaveEdit unconditionally includes the whole items array — but that is the known-deferred C29 field-LWW, and stock stays bounded since restock is count-driven with budget as clamp only; ghost-restock guards (C1 status-delegation ordering, closed→closed no-op, live stockRestored guard, -R triple guard) and WIN- tombstone revival (deleted=0 on upsert) are all intact. One real defect: the restock in StaffDashboard.completeReturn is not transactional with finalizePartialReturn — if the finalize throws or the linked order is unresolvable, stock is restored (or restored unbounded) with no budget draw-down persisted and the walk-in ticket is deleted anyway, enabling a later double restock via admin rescue-close.

confirmed.title: Return flow not gated by isReturnEligible: undelivered orders (処理中/確認済み/配送中) can be submitted as walk-in returns from a first-class UI button
confirmed.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/src/pages/ReturnItems.tsx
confirmed.repro: 1) Place an order; leave it 処理中 (before admin 受注確定/delivery). 2) Open its OrderDetail — the 返却手続き button is shown because isRentalActive only excludes キャンセル/返却済(み)/完了 (OrderDetail.tsx:218, OrderDetailDesktop.tsx:142). 3) ReturnItems only checks ownership (lines 22-29), never status, so the flow proceeds; ReturnConfirmation submits: order status → 検品待ち, WIN- ticket enters the warehouse reception queue for goods that were never delivered. The order drops out of the admin 処理中 confirmation pipeline; if staff nevertheless inspects with counted>0, finalizePartialReturn generates a -R invoice for undelivered goods (restock is correctly guarded by stockDeducted/deliveryConfirmedAt, but billing is not). Only ReturnOrders (the list page) applies isReturnEligible; deep link and OrderDetail bypass it. Staff pickup has the 未納品は回収不可 guard — the customer walk-in path has no equivalent.
confirmed.impact: Any customer can push an undelivered order into 検品待ち with two taps, breaking the admin confirmation pipeline and seeding phantom reception tickets; potential wrong -R billing if the ticket is processed.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In ReturnItems (both variants) extend the guard: allow only isReturnEligible(order.status) plus 検品待ち (to preserve the intended edit/re-submission upsert path); show the 注文が見つかりません/not-eligible screen otherwise. Mirror the same condition on the OrderDetail 返却手続き button (replace isRentalActive with isReturnEligible-based gating).
reasons: Claim confirmed, cannot refute. (1) OrderDetail.tsx:218-221 and OrderDetailDesktop.tsx:142 gate the 返却手続き button only on !キャンセル/!返却済(み)/!完了, so undelivered orders (処理中/確認済み/配送中) show it (OrderDetail.tsx:637-658 links to /return/${order.id}). (2) ReturnItems.tsx:22-29 checks ownership only — no status check in ReturnItems/ReturnItemsDesktop/ReturnShipping(+Desktop). (3) ReturnConfirmation.tsx handleSubmit (lines 32-208) has no status guard: it unconditionally pushes the WIN- walkinReturns reception ticket (lines 169-196) and sets status 検品待ち (line 199), pulling the order out of the admin 処理中 pipeline. (4) isReturnEligible (orderStatus.ts:24-28) explicitly documents 未配送=不可 but is enforced only in ReturnOrders.tsx:21 / ReturnOrdersDesktop.tsx:16 (list filter) — the OrderDetail button and deep link bypass it, so this is a genuine gap, not intentional design. (5) finalizePartialReturn (utils/returnProcessing.ts) generates -R billing with no deliveryConfirmedAt/stockDeducted guard (guards exist only on the restock side), matching the wrong-billing impact. Not in the intentional-design list and not fixed on this branch.

Claim verified at every step. (1) OrderDetail.tsx:218-221 and OrderDetailDesktop.tsx:142 compute isRentalActive excluding only キャンセル/返却済(み)/完了, so 処理中/確認済み/配送中 orders render the 返却手続き Link to /return/${order.id} (OrderDetail.tsx:652-658). (2) ReturnItems.tsx:22-29 checks ownership only — no status check; App.tsx:60-62 routes have no guard. (3) isReturnEligible (orderStatus.ts:26, whose own comment says 未配送 must be blocked) is used only in ReturnOrders.tsx:21 and ReturnOrdersDesktop.tsx:16 — the list page — so OrderDetail and deep links bypass it. (4) ReturnConfirmation.tsx:176-199 (and desktop equivalent) unconditionally pushes the WIN- walkinReturns ticket (stage: reception) and sets status 検品待ち via updateOrder, which applies patches blindly (OrderContext.tsx:130-145). (5) The 未納品は回収不可 guard exists only in the staff pickup path (MobileLiveContext.tsx:288); no equivalent exists on the customer walk-in path or the reception queue. Not covered by the intentional-design list (which sanctions ticket/billing semantics, not initiating returns on undelivered orders) and not fixed in the 160a94f batch. The bug is real: an undelivered order can be pushed into 検品待ち with a phantom reception ticket by the customer, and if staff process it with counted>0, finalizePartialReturn bills a -R order (restock is guarded, billing is not).

confirmed.title: Cross-method re-submission leaves the other pipeline's state behind (pickup→walkin keeps staffStatus=回収予定; walkin→pickup keeps the WIN- reception ticket)
confirmed.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/src/pages/ReturnConfirmation.tsx
confirmed.repro: Direction A: customer requests full-return pickup (order → status 回収中, staffStatus 回収予定, requestedReturn set). OrderDetail still shows 返却手続き (回収中 passes isRentalActive), customer redoes the flow as 直接持ち込み → walkin branch updateOrder({status:"検品待ち", returnRequestType}) never clears staffStatus/requestedReturn. requestedReturn is later cleared by finalizePartialReturn, but staffStatus survives finalization; a continuing 一部返却 order with staffStatus=回収予定 matches MobileLiveContext liveRecoveries' `daysLeft<=7 || staffStatus==="回収予定"` branch → phantom recovery job in the staff app months before rentalEnd. Direction B: customer submits walk-in (WIN- ticket, 検品待ち), then via back-navigation switches to pickup — the pickup branch (lines 136-144) has no walkinReturns cleanup, so the WIN- reception ticket stays in the warehouse queue while the order is 回収中; it is only cleaned up if the field-recovery completion path (MobileLiveContext ~510) runs.
confirmed.impact: Ghost jobs/tickets: staff may be dispatched to collect items nobody asked to be collected, and reception staff see a walk-in ticket for an order actually scheduled for pickup. Operational confusion, no billing corruption.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In the walkin branch, also clear pickup residue when present: updateOrder(order.id, { status:"検品待ち", returnRequestType, ...(order.staffStatus==="回収予定" ? { staffStatus:"", requestedReturn:{} } : {}) }). In the pickup branch, run the same walkinReturns cleanup loop as the walkin branch but WITHOUT the id!==walkinId exclusion (remove the WIN- ticket too). Same edit in ReturnConfirmationDesktop.tsx.
reasons: Verified, could not refute. Direction A: pickup branch (ReturnConfirmation.tsx:136-144) sets staffStatus=回収予定/requestedReturn; 回収中 passes isRentalActive (OrderDetail.tsx:218-221) and ReturnItems.tsx has no status guard, so the walk-in redo is reachable; its update (ReturnConfirmation.tsx:199) is a merge (OrderContext.tsx:130-145) leaving staffStatus intact; finalizePartialReturn (returnProcessing.ts:286-300) clears requestedReturn but never staffStatus; the continuing 一部返却 order then matches liveRecoveries via the staffStatus==="回収予定" branch (MobileLiveContext.tsx:280-312) → phantom recovery job. Direction B: 検品待ち also passes isRentalActive (no back-navigation even needed); pickup branch has no walkinReturns cleanup, and the WIN- ticket list renders unfiltered (MobileLiveContext.tsx:203-205, WalkInReturnFlow.tsx:107); cleanup only happens in completeRecovery (MobileLiveContext.tsx:509-513), undo, or final inspection (StaffDashboard.tsx:1076). Not on the intentional-design list and not fixed in 160a94f. Minor nit: in pure Direction A rentalEndDate was already overwritten to pickupDate (line 142), so "months before rentalEnd" requires a later extension, but the staffStatus branch bypasses the 7-day window regardless — mechanism and impact stand.

Claim verified, cannot refute. Direction A: pickup branch (ReturnConfirmation.tsx:136-144) sets staffStatus=回収予定; 回収中 passes isRentalActive (OrderDetail.tsx:218-221) so the return flow is re-enterable (ReturnItems.tsx has ownership-only guard); the walkin branch (ReturnConfirmation.tsx:199) patches only {status:"検品待ち", returnRequestType} via merging updateOrder (OrderContext.tsx:130-145), leaving staffStatus/requestedReturn behind; finalizePartialReturn clears requestedReturn but never staffStatus (returnProcessing.ts:286-300; StaffDashboard.tsx:1039-1068 extraFields don't include it); the continuing 一部返却 order then matches liveRecoveries — 一部返却 not in RECOVERY_EXCLUDED_STATUS, passes isDelivered, and line 312 `daysLeft<=7 || staffStatus==="回収予定"` fires regardless of rentalEndDate (MobileLiveContext.tsx:280-312) → phantom recovery job. Direction B: 検品待ち also passes isRentalActive; ReturnShipping.tsx:36-37/111-118 offers (even defaults to) pickup for full returns; the pickup branch has zero walkinReturns cleanup, and the staff walkin queue is the raw unfiltered collection (MobileLiveContext.tsx:203-205), so the WIN- ticket lingers until completeRecovery (MobileLiveContext.tsx:509-513) or manual processing (StaffDashboard.tsx:1076). Not covered by the intentional-design list (which addresses same-id upsert races, not cross-method residue) and not fixed on the current branch. Severity LOW (operational confusion, no billing corruption) is appropriate.

Desktop ReturnConfirmationDesktop.tsx:313 runs navigate("/orders") for the 修正する button while mobile ReturnConfirmation.tsx:300 runs navigate(-1); both render from the same /return-confirmation route switched by useIsDesktop() (ReturnConfirmation.tsx:12), so desktop users genuinely get the abandoning behavior. navigate(-1) would work on desktop too — ReturnShippingDesktop reads flow state from location.state (lines 26-28), which react-router preserves across history pops, and its own 戻る button already uses navigate(-1) (line 93). Claim verified, cannot refute. confirmed.title: Success alert shown before server confirmation: an offline walk-in submission is silently lost if the tab is closed before reconnect
confirmed.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/src/pages/ReturnConfirmation.tsx
confirmed.repro: 1) Go offline (or server briefly down). 2) Submit the walk-in return: OrderBus.push/patch write to memory+localStorage, the upserts fail with a network error and stay only in the in-memory _pendingUpserts set (orderBus.ts:367 — not persisted); the UI immediately shows 「返却を受け付けました。倉庫での検品後に内容が確定します。」 and navigates to /orders. 3) Close the tab before connectivity returns. 4) Reopen later: _pendingUpserts is empty, the poller resumes incremental sync from the stored rev, and the local-only WIN- ticket and 検品待ち patch are never re-pushed (a later authoritative full resync drops them). Customer believes the return was accepted; warehouse/admin never see it.
confirmed.impact: Silently lost return submission with a false success message — customer shows up at the warehouse with goods and no ticket. Requires offline-at-submit + tab closed before reconnect, so low frequency, but the flow is exactly the kind the codebase's own flush() API was added for.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Before showing the success dialog, await OrderBus.flush(8000) (as the staff field flows do) and on false show a 送信待ち/再試行 message instead of unconditional success; longer term, persist _pendingUpserts to localStorage so queued writes survive restarts. Apply identically in ReturnConfirmationDesktop.tsx.
reasons: Claim verified end-to-end, cannot refute. (1) ReturnConfirmation.tsx:176-207 (and desktop variant :179-210) does fire-and-forget OrderBus.push("walkinReturns")/updateOrder→patch, then unconditionally alerts 「返却を受け付けました…」 and navigates — no flush()/onSyncError. (2) orderBus.ts:367 _pendingUpserts is a memory-only Set (never persisted); a network-failed upsert stays pending only in memory (orderBus.ts:681-691, non-4xx path). (3) After tab close+reopen, _startApiPoller (orderBus.ts:562-585) resumes incremental sync from stored rev with an empty pending set; _retryPendingUpserts (403) re-sends nothing, and first-poll bulk upload is deliberately disabled (533-539), so the local-only WIN- ticket and 検品待ち patch are never re-pushed — warehouse/admin never see them. (4) A rev-regression full resync (_reloadAuthoritativeSnapshot:473-483) drops the record since the pendingLocal filter needs _pendingUpserts membership. flush() exists (orderBus.ts:923) and is used by PersonalInfo.tsx:62 and StaffDashboard.tsx:1188/1205 but not this flow; nothing in the intentional-design list covers pre-confirmation success alerts. Minor nuance: the ticket persists in the customer's own localStorage (visible locally after reload), but the server never receives it, which is the claimed impact. LOW severity is apt.

Claim confirmed, not refuted. ReturnConfirmation.tsx handleSubmit (mobile lines 176/199/202-207; desktop equivalent) fires OrderBus.push("walkinReturns")/OrderBus.patch("orders") and synchronously shows the success alert and navigates, with no flush()/onSyncError/pendingCount guard. _pendingUpserts (orderBus.ts:367) is a memory-only Set — never persisted; a network-error upsert stays pending in memory only (orderBus.ts:686-691). After tab close+reopen, _startApiPoller resumes incremental sync from the stored rev (orderBus.ts:562-585), first-poll local upload is intentionally disabled (orderBus.ts:533-535), so the local-only WIN- ticket and 検品待ち patch are never re-pushed, and a later authoritative full resync drops the ticket because retention requires _pendingUpserts membership (orderBus.ts:473-475). The customer app has no sync-error listener or offline indicator (only StaffDashboard does), so the failure is silent. Not covered by the intentional-design list and not fixed in recent commits; flush() exists for exactly this pattern and is used in PersonalInfo.tsx:62 and staff flows but not here.

confirmed.title: liveAlreadyRestored guard resolves the wrong order (undefined firestoreId match) — restock silently skipped yet order stamped stockRestored
confirmed.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/src/pages/Staff/StaffDashboard.tsx
confirmed.repro: Line 942: freshLinked = getAll("orders").find(o => o.id === linkedOrder.id || o.firestoreId === linkedOrder.firestoreId). Client-created orders never have firestoreId, so undefined === undefined matches and find() returns the FIRST firestoreId-less order in the newest-first array — effectively orders[0], not the linked order. Repro: (1) staff finalizes walk-in partial return for order A → -R order created with stockRestored:true (extraFields, StaffDashboard:1045 → returnProcessing.ts:314) and OrderBus.push prepends it to orders. (2) Staff immediately processes the next recheck-queue ticket for order B (delivered, stockDeducted, not restored). (3) In completeReturn, shouldRestock=true but freshLinked resolves to A-R → liveAlreadyRestored=true (line 944-945) → the entire restock block is skipped: no adjustProductStock, no stockIn ledger row. (4) extraFields.stockRestored=true is still written to B (condition at 1045 checks only shouldRestock), so settleReturnStock/any later restore is permanently blocked.
confirmed.impact: Physical stock returned in B is never re-entered into products.stock and cannot be recovered by any automatic path (stockRestored flag blocks restoreOrderStock and admin rescue-close). Sequential queue processing after any partial-return finalize — the normal warehouse batch workflow — triggers it deterministically. Additionally, because freshLinked virtually never points at the real linked order, the multi-device double-restock protection this guard was added for (160a94f batch) is inoperative.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Match strictly: OrderBus.getAll("orders").find(o => o.id === linkedOrder.id || (!!linkedOrder.firestoreId && o.firestoreId === linkedOrder.firestoreId)) — same guarded pattern already used in AdminFieldReportManagement.tsx:60. Optionally also condition extraFields.stockRestored on the restock actually having produced entries (restockedByItem non-empty or the no-order branch having run) rather than on shouldRestock alone.
reasons: CONFIRMED, not refuted. StaffDashboard.tsx:942 matches `o.firestoreId === linkedOrder.firestoreId` with no undefined guard. Client-created orders never have firestoreId (OrderContext.tsx:106-116/148-155 set none; orderBus.ts push:737-758 adds none; server PHP injects none; AdminDataContext.tsx:178/196 backfill is a display-only derived view never written back). So for any linkedOrder without firestoreId, find() returns the first firestoreId-less record in the newest-first array (orderBus.ts:749 prepend, :452-458 createdAt-desc sort) — i.e. orders[0], not the linked order. Repro verified: finalizing a partial return creates the -R order with stockRestored:true (StaffDashboard.tsx:1045 → returnProcessing.ts:314 ...extraFields) via addCustomOrder → OrderBus.push prepend (OrderContext.tsx:162). Processing the next recheck ticket for order B then resolves freshLinked to that -R order, liveAlreadyRestored=true (StaffDashboard.tsx:944), and the entire restock block (lines 945-987: restoreOrderStock/addStockMove/adjustStock) is skipped with restockedByItem empty. Line 1045 still stamps stockRestored:true (condition checks only shouldRestock), landing on B itself in the full-return path (returnProcessing.ts:247) or on B-R in the partial path (:314); stockLedger.restoreOrderStock refuses restock when stockRestored is set (stockLedger.ts:140-142 contract), so the physical stock is permanently lost to the ledger. The correct pattern exists in stockLedger.ts resolveLiveOrder (:61-72), which coalesces firestoreId||id into a non-empty string first — confirming StaffDashboard:942 is a defective re-implementation, not intentional design; no item in the intentional-design list covers it, and the code is unfixed at HEAD (160a94f).

CONFIRMED, not refuted. Verified end-to-end: (1) StaffDashboard.tsx:941-942 hand-rolls the live lookup as find(o => o.id === linkedOrder.id || o.firestoreId === linkedOrder.firestoreId) over OrderBus.getAll("orders") instead of using the safe resolveLiveOrder (stockLedger.ts:61-72, which coalesces firestoreId||id to a non-empty string). (2) linkedOrder comes from useOrders()/OrderContext (StaffDashboard:793), whose subscription passes raw bus records with no firestoreId backfill (OrderContext.tsx:98-99), and addOrder/addCustomOrder (OrderContext.tsx:106-116, 148-155) never set firestoreId; the api/ backend adds none. So for any post-Firestore order B, linkedOrder.firestoreId is undefined and o.firestoreId === undefined matches the FIRST firestoreId-less record in the newest-first array (push prepends, orderBus.ts:749; sync sorts seq/createdAt desc, orderBus.ts:452-458). (3) After any partial-return finalize, that first record is the just-created -R order carrying stockRestored:true (StaffDashboard:1045 → returnProcessing.ts:314 → addCustomOrder → push) — so processing the next recheck ticket for order B yields freshLinked=A-R, liveAlreadyRestored=true, and the entire restock block (StaffDashboard:945-987) is skipped: no restoreOrderStock, restockedByItem stays empty. (4) Line 1045 gates only on shouldRestock, so stockRestored:true is still stamped onto B's split (returnProcessing.ts:247 full-return path / :314 partial path), and restoreOrderStock's guard (stockLedger.ts:159) plus settleReturnStock (stockLedger.ts:229) then permanently block any later restock — the physical stock never re-enters products.stock. Also, since freshLinked essentially never resolves to the real linked order for firestoreId-less orders, the multi-device double-restock guard this code was added for (160a94f) is inoperative. Working tree clean at HEAD; no fix present; nothing in the intentional-design list covers this. The repro is the normal sequential warehouse batch workflow and is deterministic.

confirmed.title: 再検品 (reinspect) re-queues an already-finalized inspection and completeReturn re-runs the full finalize pipeline — double restock, continuing order closed, or items wiped
confirmed.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/src/pages/Staff/WalkInReturnFlow.tsx
confirmed.repro: reinspect (lines 183-205) pushes a stage:"recheck" ticket from a returnInspections history record with no idempotency marker, and StaffDashboard.completeReturn has no source==="reinspect" handling. Repro A (partial order): order O has item X qty 10; cycle 1 walk-in returns 5 → restock +5, continuing order qty 5 / stockDeductedQty 5, -R created. Staff taps 再検品 on that history card, re-counts the same 5 units, confirms: shouldRestock is true (continuing order has budget 5, no stockRestored), restoreOrderStock adds ANOTHER +5 (phantom — those units were restocked in cycle 1), then finalizePartialReturn sees returningQty=5=remaining → returningEverything → continuing order for the 5 units STILL AT THE CUSTOMER is closed 返却済 with rent cut at today (reinspect ticket has no receptionReturnDate → falls back to final-inspection date). Repro B (closed full return): reinspect and count 4 of 5 → shortage 1 → hasMissingIssues=true bypasses the empty-return skip (returnProcessing.ts:213) → full path runs updateOrder with items: split.returnedItemsList = [] (all items have returnedQuantity===quantity so returningQty=0) → order item lines wiped, totals recomputed from empty blocks, plus a false missing-compensation charge for a unit sitting in the warehouse.
confirmed.impact: One tap of a first-class UI button offered on every history card, used exactly as labeled (redo a count), silently inflates stock by the returned quantity, terminates billing for goods still on rental, or destroys a closed order's line items and fabricates compensation charges. No confirmation beyond the generic 確定 dialog distinguishes this from a normal inspection.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In StaffDashboard.completeReturn, treat walkinOrder.source === "reinspect" as record-only: push the new returnInspections record and field reports but skip both the restock block and finalizePartialReturn (or require an explicit admin correction flow). plausible.title: WIN- ticket id squatting: another authenticated customer can pre-create WIN-<victimOrderId> bound to their own order, permanently 403-ing the victim's walk-in submissions
plausible.file: /Users/matruongan/antigravity/アサヒリースレンタル・販売/public/api/store.php
plausible.repro: Attacker (valid customer token, owns order X) learns victim's internal order id V (e.g. from a shared OrderDetail URL). Attacker POSTs /store?name=walkinReturns with body {id:"WIN-"+sanitize(V), orderId:X}: ownsOrderId(X) passes (line ~180) and there is no existing record, so the squat is stored. When the victim later submits a real return, the client pushes id WIN-<V> with orderId V; the existing-record check (lines ~185-193) finds the stored ticket's orderId=X, which the victim does not own → 403 forever. Client-side the 4xx path in orderBus._upsertExternalized drops the pending write silently (regex "→ 4\d\d " matches backendSync's message), while the UI has already shown 「返却を受け付けました」 and set the order to 検品待ち — no ticket ever reaches the warehouse queue.
plausible.impact: Targeted, persistent denial of the return flow for one customer plus an inconsistent 検品待ち order with no ticket; recoverable only by staff deleting the squatted row. Exploitability is low (order ids are not exposed cross-customer; walkinReturns GET/sync are owner-scoped), hence LOW.
plausible.proposed_fix: In the walkinReturns POST branch, when the id matches the deterministic pattern ^WIN-<sanitized>$, require that it equals "WIN-" + sanitize(body.orderId) (i.e., the ticket id must be derived from an order the writer owns); alternatively require stored.orderId === body.orderId on overwrite instead of only checking writer ownership of the stored orderId.
reasons:
CONFIRMED (not refuted). The code does exactly what the claim describes, and no guard prevents it.

SERVER (public/api/store.php): line 108 `$id = (string) $body['id']` — the record id is fully client-controlled. The customer-write branch for walkinReturns (lines 168-193) validates only: (a) `body.orderId` is owned by the caller (line 180), and (b) IF a row already exists at that id, its STORED orderId is owned (lines 185-193). There is NO validation that the record id is consistent with `body.orderId`. So a customer who owns order X can POST {id:"WIN-<sanitize(V)>", orderId:X}: line 180 passes (owns X), no existing row → the INSERT at 254-259 stores the squat. The existing 185-193 check was built for the MIRROR-IMAGE attack (overwriting a victim's pre-existing ticket) and is inert against pre-creation squatting because there is no prior row. When the victim later submits at the same deterministic id WIN-<sanitize(order.id)> with orderId=V, the squat row's stored orderId=X is not owned by the victim → 403 (lines 190-191), permanently. Victim DELETE is also blocked (line 374), and the SELECT at 185 does not filter deleted=0, so even soft-deleting the squat would keep 403-ing.

CLIENT: walkinId is deterministic `WIN-<sanitize(order.id)>` (src/pages/ReturnConfirmation.tsx:169); the UI synchronously sets status 検品待ち (:199) and shows 「返却を受け付けました」 (:202-206) while the push is fire-and-forget. The 403 surfaces as message "... → 403 ..." (src/lib/backendSync.ts:49) which matches the regex /→ 4\d\d / at src/lib/orderBus.ts:687, deleting the pending write and returning — silent drop. push() sends no X-Base-Rev (baseRev only set for patch-origin writes, orderBus.ts:643-644), so it is a plain 403, not a 409 rebase.

The bug is real, not intentional design (not on the exclusion list), and not already fixed. The only mitigating factor is exploitability: order.id = `id-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)}` (src/context/OrderContext.tsx:110) is unguessable, and GET/sync are owner-scoped (store.php:58-99), so the victim's internal id V is not obtainable via any API — only via the victim voluntarily sharing their authenticated /order/:id URL (App.tsx:58). That low exploitability is a severity consideration (the claim correctly rates it LOW), not a code guard that blocks the squat, so it does not refute the finding. Root cause: server-side walkinReturns writes never enforce id↔orderId consistency.

The code gap is technically real (store.php:180 checks only body.orderId ownership and never enforces that the record id is derived from orderId, so a squat row id=WIN-<sanitize(V)>,orderId=X stores, and the victim's later write at store.php:185-193 sees stored orderId=X and 403s). However the repro cannot occur through the application. The victim's deterministic ticket id is built from the high-entropy internal order.id — `WIN-`+ (order.id || orderNumber) at ReturnConfirmation.tsx:169 / ReturnConfirmationDesktop.tsx:172 — and real orders always have order.id set (OrderContext.tsx:110,154), so the guessable orderNumber fallback never fires. order.id is `id-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)}` (OrderContext.tsx:110): a ms timestamp plus 6 base36 random chars, not brute-forceable. All cross-customer reads are owner-scoped: orders/users GET filtered to caller (store.php:58-72) and walkinReturns/returnInspections GET filtered to caller-owned orders (store.php:74-98), so an attacker has no in-app channel to learn a victim's order.id. The claim's only exposure hypothesis — a "shared OrderDetail URL" (/order/:id, App.tsx:58, which contains the raw id only in the owner's own browser) — is an out-of-band, victim-initiated self-leak of an effectively secret identifier, outside the app's cross-customer attack surface; the claim itself concedes ids are not exposed cross-customer. Without that self-leak the attacker cannot target any specific victim, so the claimed targeted persistent DoS is not reachable. Worst realistic residual is a staff-recoverable single junk row, not the asserted permanent victim lockout.
